implementation_notes: Vapor's responder chain is the route: app.middleware.use(AuditMiddleware()) registers the detour globally and the middleware must call next.respond(to:) - that call is the rejoin to the same handler - while registering it only when the configuration enables it is the toggle. Route groups give a narrower switch (app.grouped(AuditMiddleware()) for one subtree), and an AsyncMiddleware can await the next responder, so a detour failure can either abort the message or fall through to the direct leg as a deliberate policy.
pitfalls: Middleware registered without at: .beginning runs after Vapor's default middleware, which changes error responses while the detour is on.
An AsyncMiddleware that throws before calling next.respond aborts the message instead of rejoining the flow.
Route-group middleware always runs after application middleware, so registering the detour in both places executes it twice.
